item.title: Confinement-induced bound state and effective potential for microwave-shielded ultracold molecules
item.description: arXiv:2611.07230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the bound state and effective potential of microwave-shielded ultracold molecules under longitudinal confinement, which effectively creates a quasi-two-dimensional (q2D) geometry. We find that the longitudinal confinement facilitates bound-state formation in both bosonic and fermionic molecules, leading to confinement-induced bound states that are absent in free space. To describe these bound states, we establish an effective 2D potential by incorporating the full interaction effect along the longitudinal direction. Compared with other simplified 2D potentials, the effective potential accurately predicts the binding energies of ultracold molecules over a much broader parameter regime of microwave coupling and confinement strength. Remarkably, it can even predict deep bound states with binding energies well exceeding the confinement frequency. By establishing this effective potential, our work paves the way for efficiently exploring the rich low-dimensional physics of microwave-shielded ultracold molecules.
item.dc:creator: Linyi Zhang, Xiaoling Cui

item.title: Initial heat-current decay versus thermal transport at a three-body resonance in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.07615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically study kinetic relaxation and heat transport in a dilute one-dimensional spinless Fermi gas near a three-body resonance. The full vacuum amplitude of a finite-range interaction enters the linearized Boltzmann collision operator. The resonance position that maximizes the initial heat-current decay rate lies above the one that minimizes the integrated relaxation time. At higher resonance energies, coupling among momentum moments transfers heat-current weight to a slow mode. A faster initial decay can therefore coexist with slower subsequent relaxation and a larger low-frequency heat response. The dissipative responses at two resonance positions reverse their ordering at least twice as frequency increases. Bounds on the full collision operator confirm both reversals. A fourth-moment distortion exhibits the same separation of relaxation scales and provides a probe through the momentum distribution.
item.dc:creator: Yixin Guo

item.title: Universal Phase Locking from Slowly Varying Inhomogeneity in Tunnel-Coupled One-Dimensional Condensates
item.description: arXiv:2611.07657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The sine-Gordon model can be experimentally realised by tunnel-coupled one-dimensional Bose condensates. However, the experiments show relaxation to a phase-locked state, which conflicts with the predictions of the homogeneous integrable theory. Here we combine the truncated Wigner approximation with an asymptotic analysis, and show that this locking is produced by a slowly varying density profile through a universal mechanism, whereby the relative phase near the density maximum drifts towards zero. We show that this drift is already present in the linearised theory and its timescale is determined by the density curvature alone, while it is independent of the tunnel coupling. Rescaling time by the relaxation time scale collapses the dynamics for different system sizes and density profiles, while non-linearity suppresses the excitation returning from the edges.
item.dc:creator: Bence Fitos, G\'abor Tak\'acs

item.title: Coherent phase slips in coupled rings: from weak to strong interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.08168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the coherent transfer of circulation between two weakly coupled lattice rings of ultracold bosons, in which a persistent current initially prepared in one ring oscillates back and forth between the rings without net transfer of particles. Combining Bose--Hubbard simulations with their Gross--Pitaevskii and quantum phase model limits, we show that similar current oscillations arise from two distinct microscopic mechanisms. At weak interactions, particles in each occupied momentum mode tunnel independently between the rings, leading to a transfer time inversely proportional to the inter-ring tunnelling, extensive particle-number fluctuations and entanglement distributed over many Schmidt components; this mode-exchange dynamics is suppressed by self-trapping as the interactions increase. At stronger interactions and large filling, in the phase-dominated regime, circulation is instead transferred through a second-order collective process between many-body persistent-current states, with a transfer time scaling as the inverse square of the inter-ring tunnelling in the weak-link limit. Number fluctuations then remain of order one instead of growing with the particle number, and within each number sector the system evolves into coherent superpositions of two many-body configurations, distinguished by which ring carries the circulation. The entanglement accessible under number-conserving operations therefore reaches up to approximately one bit. We propose a quench protocol to prepare the initial state and estimate transfer times within reach of current ring-lattice experiments, identifying coupled rings as a platform to study coherent quantum phase slips and to manipulate persistent-current states.
item.dc:creator: Axel Perez-Obiol, Malcolm G. Boshier, Luigi Amico, Juan Polo

item.title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.08447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment. Here, we investigate the wavepacket and entanglement dynamics induced by an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field. The wavepacket undergoes non-Abelian non-compact Bloch oscillations, in which the spectrum of an auxiliary one-dimensional quantum problem determines the transition between stable oscillations and unstable amplification. In the unstable adiabatic regime, the wavepacket probes an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ topological defect, and its amplification is determined solely by a hyperbolic solid angle in Minkowski space. Threading an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field through a bosonic tight-binding model yields the bosonic Kitaev model, whose volume or super-volume entanglement scaling is governed by the stability of the gauge field. We further propose an experimental realization of an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field in a spinor condensate. Our results can be generalized to other non-compact groups and higher dimensions, providing a geometric framework for entanglement control, selective amplification, and engineering energy transfer.
item.dc:creator: Chenwei Lv

item.title: Flat-band systems: A platform to realize the moments of Quantum Metric
item.description: arXiv:2611.08479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum metric is a fundamental geometric property of Bloch bands that governs a wide range of physical phenomena, yet experimentally accessing it remains challenging. We show that the momentum-space variation of the quantum metric can be probed through the real-space dynamics of a Gaussian wave packet prepared in an isolated flat band. Following the application of a weak constant force, we demonstrate analytically that the leading order change in the wave-packet variance is linear in time and contains a contribution proportional to the wave-packet averaged gradient of the quantum-metric trace. This geometric contribution remains finite despite the absence of band dispersion. We illustrate the effect using a gapped Lieb lattice with an exactly flat middle band and vanishing Berry curvature, allowing the quantum-metric contribution to the spreading to be isolated. The numerical results agree with the analytical prediction and confirm the quantum-metric contribution to the wave-packet spreading. The required lattice preparation, tunable hopping amplitudes, applied force, and density measurements are compatible with established ultracold-atom techniques, providing a possible platform for observing the predicted response. Our results establish wave-packet spreading as a dynamical probe of quantum geometry in flat-band systems.
item.dc:creator: Rishi Gangadhar, Binayyak Roy, Vito Scarola, Sumanta Tewari

item.title: Probing Non-Abelian Topology through Quench Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.07456v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quench dynamics offer valuable insights to topological matter, wherein the emergent topological phenomena serve as a dynamic probe to the topology of static Hamiltonians. While such a practice has been widely applied to detect the Abelian band topology or the Euler-class topology of band nodes, little is known regarding the quench dynamics of non-Abelian topological insulators in multiband systems, where the intertwining geometry of all eigenstates necessitates the description of noncommutative topological charges. Here we propose a quench protocol for non-Abelian topological insulators, so that the underlying topology can be systematically probed using dynamic signatures. Specifically, we develop a band-projection scheme to extract the gap-resolved topology from dynamic skyrmions in the emergent quasimomentum--time manifolds of the quench processes. These skyrmions are characterized by a series of gap-resolved dynamic Chern numbers, which enable us to reconstruct the full non-Abelian topology of the post-quench Hamiltonian, including the global non-Abelian topological charge and edge-state patterns under the open-boundary condition. Our proposal offers dynamical access to non-Abelian topology in multiband systems, and can be readily implemented using photons or cold atoms.
item.dc:creator: Zhenming Zhang, Tianyu Li, Wei Yi

item.title: Fermi-volume anomaly in quartet condensates
item.description: arXiv:2611.07601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the relation between density and Fermi volume in a four-component Fermi system with quartet order. For a regular zero-temperature branch without pair order, we express the correction to the Fermi-volume count in terms of the response of the Luttinger-Ward functional to a phase winding of the quartet source. Its leading term is a weighted difference between four-particle and four-hole states. For a Gaussian vertex and parabolic dispersion, we find that the correction expands the Fermi volume in one dimension and contracts it in three dimensions in the parameter range studied. The sign in two dimensions depends on the momentum cutoff. We solve the one-dimensional Dyson equation at fixed density and compare the counting correction obtained from the Fermi points with that evaluated from the dressed spectra at low temperature. At fixed quartet amplitude and peak normalization of the vertex, the correction depends strongly on the vertex width, whereas the fermionic entropy changes little. We also examine the linear pairing response, which can limit the continuation of the unpaired branch to zero temperature.
item.dc:creator: Yixin Guo

item.title: Asymptotic analysis of the dynamical field-field correlation function of the impenetrable Bose gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.08350v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotic behaviour of the two-point correlation function of fields of the impenetrable Bose gas in equilibrium states characterized by a quasi-momentum distribution (or filling fraction). This includes, in particular, the cases of Gibbs and generalized Gibbs ensembles. The overall structure of the asymptotic expansion depends on the number of Fermi points, those points for which the quasi-momentum distribution takes the value $1/2$. The leading asymptotic behaviour is determined by a relaxation rate, a logarithmic correction term and an amplitude for which we provide simple and explicit expressions. In the case of two Fermi points the first sub-leading correction is calculated as well.
item.dc:creator: Frank G\"ohmann, Karol K. Kozlowski, Mikhail D. Minin, Alexander Wei{\ss}e

item.title: Sound waves in a backreaction-affected analogue spacetime: acoustic metric, mass, and correlations in Bose-Einstein condensates
item.description: arXiv:2512.24233v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Analogue gravity treats sound as a field on an effective spacetime set by the background flow, but quantum fluctuations feed back on this background. Whether a condensate modified by such backreaction still defines a spacetime for the quantum field remains open. Using a number-conserving expansion of a Bose-Einstein condensate, we show that in the sound-wave and eikonal approximations the first-order phase fluctuation propagates on an acoustic metric of the backreaction-corrected condensate and acquires a spacetime-dependent mass that cannot be absorbed into the metric. For a finite, quasi-one-dimensional gas after an interaction quench, backreaction enhances the equal-point phase correlation by about $10\%$ in the bulk and up to $20\%$ near the walls while the depletion remains below $2\%$; the bulk enhancement survives finite imaging resolution.
item.dc:creator: Sang-Shin Baak, Hyun-Yong Lee

item.title: Kelvin-Helmholtz and counter-superflow instabilities driven by differential effective rotation in a three-component Bose-Einstein condensate
item.description: arXiv:2603.19207v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Interfacial hydrodynamic instabilities in multicomponent superfluids provide a versatile platform to explore nonequilibrium quantum dynamics beyond classical fluid analogues. We study dynamical interfacial instabilities in a quasi-two-dimensional three-component Bose-Einstein condensate confined in a harmonic trap, where differential effective rotation between neighboring components is generated through selective phase imprinting. A component with an imprinted vorticity $l_j$ acquires an azimuthal phase winding $\phi_j = l_j\theta$, producing a superfluid velocity $v_\theta(r_j) = l_j\hbar/mr_j$ at interface radius $r_j$ and an effective angular velocity $\Omega_j^{\mathrm{eff}} = l_j\hbar/mr_j^2$. The differential effective rotation $\Delta\Omega_j^{\mathrm{eff}} = \Omega_j^{\mathrm{eff}} - \Omega_{j+1}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ between neighboring components constitutes the sole driver of interfacial shear and the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability (KHI). Three instability regimes are examined: KHI in the strongly immiscible limit, counter-superflow instability in the partially miscible regime, and a parameter window where both mechanisms coexist. A hydrodynamic pressure-balance model is derived, showing that the KHI onset condition depends only on $\Delta\Omega_j^{\mathrm{eff}}$. Time-dependent Gross-Pitaevskii simulations and a Bogoliubov-de Gennes analysis identify the dominant unstable modes, whose spatial structures are consistent with the observed density modulations. The dominant azimuthal mode is set by a competition between shear-driven destabilization and surface-tension stabilization, confirmed by numerical simulations with different imprinted vorticities. The results show that a three-component condensate with two tunable interfaces provides a controlled platform for studying multicomponent quantum hydrodynamics, with instability dynamics significantly richer than those of binary mixtures.
item.dc:creator: Susovan Giri, Arpana Saboo, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Vipin, Sonjoy Majumder

item.title: Emergent thermal behavior, synchronization, and non-Hermitian phase transitions in driven-dissipative photon condensates
item.description: arXiv:2603.21927v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Driven-dissipative Bose-Einstein condensates of photons in optical resonators have been shown theoretically to exist as a long-lived, yet metastable state stabilized by a ghost attractor, despite continuous driving [Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 053402 (2025)]. Here we analyze the properties of this metastable condensate as well as the relaxation dynamics into and out of this state by means of the Lindblad master-equation approach, treating the condensate and the equal-time, noncondensed fluctuations on the same footing. Despite its nonequilibrium origin, the quasistationary condensate exhibits thermal behavior in that the order-parameter fluctuations scale with system size as in thermodynamic equilibrium, and the photon-number distribution in multimode resonators is in excellent agreement with a Bose-Einstein distribution. A linear stability analysis further reveals the presence of several exceptional points, resulting in multiple non-Hermitian phase transitions associated with the relaxation dynamics into and out of the metastable condensate. These behaviors reconcile apparently contradictory experimental results.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Janning, Roman Kramer, Aya Abouelela, Michael Turaev, Johann Kroha, Sayak Ray

item.title: Ground state of the Hubbard model with spin-dependent linear potential
item.description: arXiv:2604.24068v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the competition between attractive spin-spin interactions and spin-separating external forces in the ground state of a one-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model. We consider a lattice with open boundary conditions, subject to a linear external potential whose gradient is opposite for the two spin components, so that each spin species sees a potential minimum at a different end of the lattice. Using density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations, we map the ground-state density distributions and the number of doubly occupied sites as a function of the potential gradient $\beta$ and interaction strength. We identify three distinct regimes separated by critical threshold gradients: (i) a small-$\beta$ regime where fermion pairing remains robust against the external potential; (ii) an intermediate-$\beta$ phase-separated regime characterized by a staircase-like decrease in the doublon number, corresponding to the successive, one-by-one breaking of bound pairs; and (iii) a large-$\beta$ regime where the two spin components are completely spatially separated. We complement the numerical results with a phenomenological model and a local-density approximation analysis, from which we derive closed-form analytical estimates for these critical threshold values. We also verify that the staircase structure persists under additional harmonic confinement. Our results are directly testable in cold-atom experiments, and demonstrate that a spin-dependent linear potential enables precise, integer-level control of the number of bound fermion pairs.
item.dc:creator: Jacek Dobrzyniecki, Thomas Busch

item.title: Dimensional crossover in ultradilute Bose-Bose liquid mixtures
item.description: arXiv:2607.25558v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study ultradilute $^{39}$K Bose-Bose bulk mixtures and droplets in an external harmonic potential that confines them in one spatial direction towards the two-dimensional (2D) limit. Equations of state for several confinements are obtained with quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) at $T=0$, using interaction potentials that include information on the $s$-wave scattering length $a$ and the effective range $r_{\rm eff}$. Performing the calculations using two different interaction potential models we have determined the range of confinements for which equations of state are universal in terms of $a$ and $r_{\rm eff}$. Based on the QMC equation of state, we develop a 2D QMC density functional for each confinement strength and use it together with the local density approximation to determine properties of the self-bound drops. For moderate squeezing, energies and droplet profiles obtained using the 2D QMC functional agree well with those obtained using 3D functionals, while offering a substantial reduction in computational cost, and a consistent approach in crossover to 2D. Noticeably, our results approach 2D mean-field (MF) + Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) predictions only for the most strongly confined systems for which universality in terms of $a$ and $r_{\rm eff}$ is observed. This implies a very narrow range of confinements for which 2D LHY functionals are applicable, which affects the study of vortices using 2D functionals.
item.dc:creator: Leandra Vranje\v{s} Marki\'c, Ivan Popari\'c, Kre\v{s}imir D\v{z}elalija, Petar Stipanovi\'c, Jordi Boronat

item.title: Multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices
item.description: arXiv:2609.36554v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the ground-state and dynamical properties of multicomponent interacting anyons confined in a one-dimensional (1D) optical lattice. Adopting the Anyon-Hubbard model, we explore spin and charge correlations as functions of interaction strength and the anyonic statistical parameter. Our results demonstrate that multicomponent effects combined with fractional exchange statistics substantially reshape both charge and spin correlations. For fractional exchange statistics, the canonical symmetric shell structure with prominent singularities in the spinor fermionic momentum distribution undergoes notable structural reconstruction, exhibiting emergent asymmetry, new spectral peaks, and broadened singular features. Unlike the Tonks-Girardeau bosonic gas, pseudobosons, representing a limiting case of anyons, cease to display a dominant zero-momentum peak. Instead, a quasi-fermionic shell structure emerges with finite-momentum peaks, whose locations are modulated by lattice site occupancy and interaction strength. The structure factor of spin correlations uncovers antiferromagnetic ordering in spinor anyon systems, with correlation magnitudes tunable by anyonic exchange statistics. Furthermore, quench dynamics analysis reveals the statistical phase parameter as an effective tuning knob. It enables the switching of dipole oscillations between underdamped and overdamped relaxation regimes and governs overall cloud expansion dynamics. Our findings pave the way for exploring statistics-driven ground-state and dynamical phase transitions in spinor anyon systems.
item.dc:creator: Sagarika Basak, Xi-Wen Guan, Han Pu

item.title: Generalized Effective Spin-Chain formalism for multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices
item.description: arXiv:2609.36555v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a generalized effective spin-chain (GESC) formalism for strongly interacting multicomponent anyons in a one-dimensional (1D) optical lattice. By mapping particle motion onto spinless fermions and spin states onto an ordered chain, this framework provides a spin-charge-separated perspective on the physical effects of fractional exchange statistics. In the strong-interaction regime, the leading-order charge Hamiltonian becomes independent of the statistical phase; instead, virtual tunneling through doubly occupied states directly imprints this phase on the spin-exchange coefficients. The GESC formalism captures ground-state properties of the full Anyon-Hubbard model reported in S.~Basak, X.-W.~Guan, and H.~Pu, unpublished manuscript (2026), and reveals that their statistical dependence is predominantly encoded in the explicit anyonic structure of the observables rather than the underlying spin ground state. This formalism uncovers that, out of equilibrium, successive spin exchanges accumulate direction-dependent phases; the resulting interference drives crossover from dispersive to localized impurity transport and generates inversion-asymmetric propagation at intermediate statistics. Suppressed expansion persists for identical and distinguishable impurities, with differences in propagation governed by the interplay between impurity identity and interaction anisotropy. Ultimately, GESC offers a versatile, computationally efficient theoretical framework that connects macroscopic dynamics to microscopic virtual exchange processes, conferring a unique spin-charge-separated vantage for resolving how fractional exchange statistics survives strong interactions and manifests distinctly across static and dynamical regimes.
item.dc:creator: Sagarika Basak, Xi-Wen Guan, Han Pu

item.title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Quantum Processors: Simulating Fermions, Bosons, and Gauge Fields
item.description: arXiv:2409.03747v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Key to solving many societally-relevant problems in materials science, quantum chemistry and nuclear physics is understanding their fundamental microscopic quantum behaviour. All of these problems can be phrased as fermionic (e.g. electrons) and bosonic particles (e.g. lattice vibrations, photons) interacting with each other. However, solving these systems of strongly-interacting fermions and bosons is out of reach for classical computers and also non-error-corrected qubit-only quantum computers. In this paper, we introduce a hybrid qubit and bosonic-oscillator quantum-simulation framework, which is so efficient that it could simulate some of these strongly-correlated problems even without error correction. Specifically, we leverage the available universal bosonic gate set with O(1) operations per gate as a function of the bosonic cutoff. This enables our framework to provide exact decompositions of higher-order fermion-boson interactions, including notoriously challenging terms such as (2+1)D gauge theories. We show how to compile dynamics, ancilla-free partial error detection, non-local observable measurement, and ground state energy estimation using both qubit-boson variational quantum eigensolvers and quantum signal processing. We introduce a "post-qubit quantum advantage" experiment which is both out of reach of near-term qubit-only quantum computers and classical computers. We develop a new qubit-based algorithm for simulating a beamsplitter which scales as almost-linear with boson number cutoff Nmax, asymptotically outperforming previously-known qubit methods. Our framework can be used in superconducting, as well as trapped-ion and neutral-atom hardware. This work establishes digital hybrid qubit-boson quantum simulation as a promising and advantageous method for solving the many challenging strongly correlated fermion-boson models of relevance to science and technology.
item.dc:creator: Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan K\"uhn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin DeMarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, Steven M. Girvin

item.title: Observation of hysteresis in an isolated quantum system of disordered Heisenberg spins
item.description: arXiv:2508.18197v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We find energy-dependent hysteresis in an isolated Heisenberg quantum spin system, similar to thermomagnetic hysteresis in canonical spin glasses in contact with a thermal reservoir. Analogous to zero-field cooling and field cooling in conventional magnetic materials, an annealing protocol is devised to control the energy in an isolated system. Depending on the strength of disorder, the susceptibilities at zero field bifurcate at a specific energy, which signals the presence of different magnetic regimes. This behavior is apparent both in a numerical simulation by exact diagonalization of the Heisenberg Hamiltonian with twelve particles, as well as in an experiment with thousands of Rydberg atoms representing dipolar interacting quantum spins. The annealing protocols open a new path to explore the energy-dependent phase structure of spin systems at low energies. Our observation of a nonthermal metastable regime might indicate the existence of a phase transition to a novel state of isolated quantum spins.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Hornung, Eduard J. Braun, Sebastian Geier, Titus Franz, Gerhard Z\"urn, Matthias Weidem\"uller

item.title: Generating entangled polaritonic condensates by pumping with entangled pairs of photons
item.description: arXiv:2602.22778v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the steady state of two single-mode, uniform, spatially separated polaritonic condensates exposed to resonant pumping with entangled pairs of photons in the presence of incoherent exciton reservoirs created by nonresonant optical pumping. We demonstrate the principal possibility of driving the system to an entangled state despite its exposure to noises arising from the excitonic reservoirs and photon leakage through the microcavity mirrors. We estimate the minimum pair-induced polariton influx required to drive the system into a steady state that violates the partial-transpose criterion for entanglement. Furthermore, we trace the evolution of the system after a sudden switch-off of the entangled pumping. Our analysis provides estimates for the entanglement lifetime in a system of two exciton-polariton condensates.
item.dc:creator: N. A. Asriyan, A. A. Elistratov, A. V. Kavokin

item.title: Planckian dissipation from classical hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2605.19450v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hydrodynamics describes the long-time, long-distance dynamics of interacting quantum systems by classical equations, yet at low temperature quantum fluctuations might eventually invalidate this classical picture. Here we ask what it takes for a quantum system to sustain a consistently classical hydrodynamic description. Our starting point is the quantum fluctuation-dissipation theorem which, when read in the time domain, acts as a blurring of the fine details of correlation functions on a Planckian time-scale. We analyse how this blurring interacts with the diffusive large-deviation form of correlators assuming the existence of a hydrodynamic light cone velocity, and show that the interior of the cone splits into a classical region, where correlation and response satisfy the classical fluctuation-dissipation relation, and a quantum region, where they deviate sharply from it. We illustrate the mechanism on three phenomenological hydrodynamic equations - diffusion, telegraph and diffusive-telegraph. Preserving a finite classical region as the temperature is lowered forces the current relaxation rate to be bounded from above by the Planckian rate. This bound connects to bounds on diffusivity, equilibration time and shear viscosity. In this way, a Planckian bound on dissipation emerges not as a quantum constraint on microscopic dynamics, but as the price a system pays to remain describable by classical hydrodynamics down to low temperatures.
item.dc:creator: Laura Foini, Jorge Kurchan, Silvia Pappalardi
